instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Join tickets and events returning all child rows with parent title
output: SELECT c.*, p.title FROM tickets c JOIN events p ON c.event_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Left join tickets to events keeping all tickets rows
output: SELECT c.*, p.title FROM tickets c LEFT JOIN events p ON c.event_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Right join tickets to events keeping all events rows
output: SELECT c.*, p.title FROM tickets c RIGHT JOIN events p ON c.event_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Count tickets records per title
output: SELECT p.title, COUNT(c.id) FROM events p LEFT JOIN tickets c ON p.id = c.event_id GROUP BY p.title;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Sum price per title
output: SELECT p.title, SUM(c.price) FROM events p JOIN tickets c ON p.id = c.event_id GROUP BY p.title;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
events rows that have no matching tickets
output: SELECT p.title FROM events p LEFT JOIN tickets c ON p.id = c.event_id WHERE c.id IS NULL;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Full outer join tickets and events
output: SELECT * FROM tickets c FULL OUTER JOIN events p ON c.event_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Cross join tickets and events
output: SELECT * FROM tickets CROSS JOIN events;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Join and filter tickets rows where price > 100
output: SELECT c.*, p.title FROM tickets c JOIN events p ON c.event_id = p.id WHERE c.price > 100;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Average price per title for title having more than 3 children
output: SELECT p.title, AVG(c.price) FROM events p JOIN tickets c ON p.id = c.event_id GROUP BY p.title HAVING COUNT(c.id) > 3;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Max price per title
output: SELECT p.title, MAX(c.price) FROM events p JOIN tickets c ON p.id = c.event_id GROUP BY p.title;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Rows joining a city starting with 'N' in title
output: SELECT c.*, p.title FROM tickets c JOIN events p ON c.event_id = p.id WHERE p.title LIKE 'N%';

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Join with alias and order by price desc
output: SELECT c.id, p.title AS detail, c.price FROM tickets c JOIN events p ON c.event_id = p.id ORDER BY c.price DESC;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Left join showing nulls for title when unmatched
output: SELECT c.*, p.title FROM tickets c LEFT JOIN events p ON c.event_id = p.id;

instruction:
Schema: tickets(id, event_id, price) and events(id, title)
Grouped join returning count and sum together
output: SELECT p.title, COUNT(c.id) AS cnt, SUM(COALESCE(c.price,0)) AS tot FROM events p LEFT JOIN tickets c ON p.id = c.event_id GROUP BY p.title;
